memory_candidates.content: A verification gate that runs heavy work (a full deploy plus an entire test suite) immediately before taking the measurement it judges can self-inflict the very failure it then blames on the batch. The fix pattern is a two-stage additive filter applied to any candidate 'new finding' before it is allowed to block: (1) a CONFIRMATION filter -- re-run the check once more on a now-settled system and keep only findings that reproduce (a real regression reproduces; a load-induced flake does not, so this can only shrink the candidate set, never weaken the gate); (2) an ATTRIBUTION filter -- drop confirmed findings that positively name an identifier absent from the batch's own changed-files set, but MUST stay fail-safe toward blocking: a finding naming no identifier at all can never be proven unrelated and must still block, or the filter degrades into a blanket disable. Implemented in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh (deploy_baseline_confirm_new_findings, deploy_baseline_unattributable_findings).

An unquoted bash heredoc delimiter (<<EOF instead of <<'EOF') lets backticks inside the heredoc body be interpreted as command substitution at write time, silently deleting or corrupting any backtick-quoted code identifiers/paths in the written file's content when those commands fail or produce unexpected output. Always use a quoted delimiter (<<'EOF') for heredocs whose body contains backtick-quoted markdown (code spans like `some/path.sh`) unless intentional interpolation is required -- verify by grepping the written file for the expected literal text immediately after writing.
